A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBM noise study with the same title and authors. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CUB and AwA2 experiments on annotation noise, concept interventions, SAM training, and CBM variants, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds conditional-noise, uncertainty–susceptibility, and seed-stability results.

M1.justification: The SAM training objective, susceptibility criterion, and entropy/UCP intervention procedure remain unchanged. The additions evaluate and explain the existing framework without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds a CUB scenario with dependent concept and target corruption, where concept noise occurs only when the target label is corrupted. CUB, AwA2, and the existing classification tasks remain; the new discussion of language modalities does not report evaluation on another modality.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds UCP and CCTP alongside Random in the direct comparison with susceptibility-guided intervention. These methods already appeared elsewhere in v1, but their membership in this comparison is new. Table 7 retains the LSR and SL baselines.

E3.justification: The added conditional-noise experiment corrupts target labels first and restricts concept corruption to affected samples. V2 also adds a comparison of susceptible concept sets across noise realizations. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, training budgets, hyperparameter settings, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends tests of the central mechanism: conditional-noise correlations in D.4, an AwA2 replication in D.11, susceptibility stability across seeds in D.13, and susceptible-set SAM comparisons across CBM variants in Section 5. These examine dependence assumptions, generalization, and structural stability beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions state three random seeds and retain the existing ± reporting. V2 newly displays separate Seed1–Seed3 susceptibility results in Figure 20. This adds seed-specific reporting without establishing an increased run count or a new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical values. Added results include susceptible-set correlations of 0.646, 0.624, and 0.549 under conditional noise in Figure 16, and 0.540, 0.355, and 0.175 on AwA2 in Figure 18, at noise rates 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 respectively. V2 also adds intervention curves, seed-specific outcomes, and variant-specific susceptible-set results; these supplement the established findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, SAM regularization derivation, and ranking-recovery proofs in Appendices A and B are substantively unchanged. V2 adds explanatory prose connecting predicted concepts to training noise and changes cross-reference wording, without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and concluding claims retain the same scope: characterize noise damage, identify susceptible concepts and representation misalignment, and mitigate these effects through SAM and uncertainty-guided intervention. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new Discussion substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. It justifies independent corruption as a control, acknowledges limitations of the conditional-noise test, explains relative resistance to target noise through the linear predictor, qualifies SAM benefits across variants, and discusses possible modality transfer. New appendix passages interpret cross-seed consistency as structural sensitivity and AwA2 correlations as evidence of generality.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly supplies a code repository link. The added analyses describe conditional corruption and seed-specific noise checks. Existing hardware, training schedules, hyperparameters, and search tables are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Arazo et al. on label-noise modeling, Zhang et al. on mixup, and Tan et al. on language-model concept bottlenecks. These support limited additions concerning SAM's positioning and possible language applications; the existing CBM related-work comparison remains.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a Discussion before the now-renumbered Conclusion, reorders several Appendix D subsections, and adds explanatory passages and limited language edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 9 gains UCP/CCTP curves and an expanded legend. New Figures 16, 18, and 20 display conditional-noise correlations, AwA2 correlations, and seed stability. Existing figures and tables undergo limited relocation and renumbering; the other existing graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The conditional-noise, AwA2, and seed-stability checks strengthen support for the susceptible-concept explanation. The expanded discussion and code access information also improve transparency. These gains are incremental: the main benchmarks and proofs remain unchanged, and the conditional-noise experiment establishes correlation rather than directly demonstrating intervention effectiveness, limiting the strength of the accompanying robustness interpretation.
